archetype.name: Gunslinger (play-extender)
archetype.definition: A rhythm-and-timing passer who has always lived on extending plays, attacking the intermediate middle and accepting sacks and turnovers as the cost of chasing big plays, and who tops out when the pocket holds and the quick game moves the chains.

report.headline: Sacks and stalled close-game dropbacks, not accuracy, have sunk Mayfield's season
report.take:
Mayfield's career is a known shape: a high-variance passer whose good years (2020, 2023, 2024) came when the offense let him throw on time and whose bad ones (2019, 2021, 2022) came with pressure, bad throws and sacks. 2026 so far sits with the bad ones. His -0.205 EPA per dropback ranks 41st of 45, and his offense looks it: the Bucs are 30th in pass EPA and 26th in pass rate over expected. This is a run-first team built around a top-three defense, and the passing game has been the weak spot.

What's sinking him is mostly not accuracy. His CPOE of 1.26 ranks 20th and is 3.4 points better than last year, and when he gets the ball 10 to 19 yards downfield he's been efficient (+0.228 EPA per attempt). The damage is in the drive-killers: a 10.8% sack rate (42nd), a pressure-to-sack rate of 44.8% that ranks 37th of 38, and a 2.99-second time to throw that's up from 2.85 last year while his aggressiveness has dropped from 16.4% to 12.5%. He's holding the ball longer and throwing into tight windows less, which is the worst mix for a quarterback whose sacks have always been the price of playing on schedule. Add 24 throws behind the line that completed at 91.7% and still averaged -0.243 EPA, plus a 17.8% bad-throw rate (35th), and drives die early.

The numbers also hide how lopsided the game-state picture is. In one-score games he's at -0.445 EPA on 89 plays, an EPA total of -39.6, worse than his entire season. Trailing by nine or more he's been sharp (+0.288, 87% completions). Third downs (-0.359 EPA, 6 sacks, 32.4% converted at an average of 8.5 to go) and the no-huddle (-0.906) are where it's ugliest. Some of this is schedule: Minnesota (now 1st in defensive EPA) blitzed him 26 times, Cleveland ranks 7th, and three lost fumbles in the opener at Cincinnati dragged a 23-of-28, +14 CPOE game into the red. That fumble cluster is noise. The Cleveland game, a -13.6 EPA loss as an 8.5-point favorite with only 12.5% pressure and a 21.2% bad-throw rate, is not, and it's the one that worries me.

The return from three missed starts tells us little: 11 attempts in a 43-13 rout of Carolina, where the run game and defense did the work. His track record says the efficiency should climb back toward his 2025 level (0.089 EPA per play, 26 TDs). But he's at 2.8% TDs against a 4.5% league average, his best receiver by usage is out, and his right tackle is out. The near-term case is a modest rebound, not a 2024-style turnaround.

strengths.title: Intermediate accuracy is still there
strengths.body: His ball placement on throws that matter hasn't left. CPOE ranks 20th and is up from last year, and the 10-to-19-yard window has been his most productive area, with his best per-target results going to Chris Godwin Jr. That matches the 2023-2024 version of him, so it's sustainable, though 26 intermediate attempts is a small sample.

strengths.title: Legs still bail out broken plays
strengths.body: He has scrambled on 7% of dropbacks for +0.237 EPA a scramble and four first downs on nine tries. That's the good side of his play-extending style, and the 382 rushing yards he posted last year (9th) say it's a real part of his game rather than a fluke. It doesn't yet pay for the sacks that come with holding the ball, but it gives the offense a floor when protection breaks.

concerns.title: Pressure turns into sacks too often
concerns.body: He takes sacks on 44.8% of pressured dropbacks, 37th of 38, and a 10.8% sack rate overall. Taking sacks is a career trait (0.391 pressure-to-sack last year, 44th), the cost of extending plays. But this season the longer time to throw isn't buying downfield shots, since his aggressiveness fell. With right tackle Luke Goedeke (100% of snaps) out, this is the number most likely to stay bad in the short term.

concerns.title: One-score and third-down collapse
concerns.body: Almost all of his negative value came with the game in the balance: -39.6 EPA in one-score situations and -0.359 per play on third down, where six of his sacks came. Part of that is opponent quality (Minnesota and Cleveland rank 1st and 7th on defense). But the drop-off is too steep to be schedule alone, and the comfortable-lead and blowout splits that look good are tiny samples played against softer coverage.

concerns.title: Quick game and bad throws
concerns.body: The easy throws aren't easy: passes behind the line average -0.243 EPA despite near-perfect completion, and Bucky Irving's 17 targets have produced -0.221 a target. Combined with a bad-throw rate of 17.8%, up from 15.1% last year, the offense can't stay on schedule. Screen design is partly a scheme issue, but the bad-throw spike in a low-pressure Cleveland game is on him.

trend.note: Negative passing EPA in each of his first three starts, with the worst coming against Cleveland, then a small positive line on 11 attempts in a Carolina blowout after his three-game absence. His last three games run slightly below his season rates, so there's no real upswing yet.

nextGame.headline: Thin Falcons secondary, but Mayfield plays without Egbuka and Goedeke
nextGame.body:
Atlanta is a middling defense overall (13th in EPA, 9th against the pass) that gives quarterbacks yardage: 276 passing yards a game, 27th. It's also built to punish exactly what's hurting him. The Falcons are 9th in QB hit rate, and they're 5th against deep passes, which takes away the shot plays he's completed at 21.4%. They don't finish sacks well (21st in sack rate), which is the opening for a quarterback whose pressures keep turning into sacks. The soft spot is the second receiver, where Atlanta allows 0.56 EPA a target (29th), and backs catching passes do well against it (31st).

Availability cuts both ways. Atlanta is without corners Avieon Terrell and Billy Bowman Jr. (each around half the snaps) and starting linebacker Divine Deablo, so its coverage depth is thin underneath and outside. Tampa loses Emeka Egbuka, his most-targeted receiver, to a concussion, which moves Godwin into the lead role and pushes Ted Hurst III (-0.222 EPA a target) up the depth chart. Goedeke's absence at tackle is the bigger problem for this matchup, given Atlanta's hit rate. Both teams lean on the run (Atlanta -6.8 pass rate over expected, Tampa -3.7), and the Book's 46.5 total and TB -2.5 point to a close game. That's the game state where he's struggled most. The forecast is early and shows a chance of thunderstorms with light rain; it's not worth building on yet.

keyMatchups.title: Replacement right tackle vs. Atlanta's pressure
keyMatchups.body: Goedeke has played every snap this season, and Atlanta gets home on QB hits at a top-ten rate. Mayfield's sack problem is the main reason his EPA is negative, so a weaker right side against a defense that hits the quarterback is the matchup that decides his day.

keyMatchups.title: Intermediate throws vs. depleted corners
keyMatchups.body: His intermediate passing has been his best area, and Atlanta is missing two rotation corners and allows big efficiency to secondary receivers. With the deep shots likely capped, the 10-to-19-yard window to Godwin and the second receiver is where the yards are.

keyMatchups.title: Run-heavy, one-score script
keyMatchups.body: Both offenses lean run and the spread is under a field goal, so expect a tight game and modest pass volume. That's a problem for a passer at -0.445 EPA in one-score situations, and it limits his ceiling even if the efficiency improves.

nextGame.watch: How often pressure ends in a sack versus a scramble or a throwaway with a backup at right tackle. If he keeps the sack rate down, the depleted Atlanta secondary gives him room to post his first good full game.

restOfSeason.body:
Expect a partial rebound rather than a return to 2024. His accuracy, intermediate passing and scrambling hold up against his career, his 2.8% TD rate is far below anything he's posted as a Buccaneer, and the opening-game fumbles won't keep repeating. So his EPA should drift up from the bottom five toward the league's middle. Volume caps the upside: Tampa runs more than the situation predicts, the defense keeps games low-scoring, and the sack rate, a career trait made worse by longer holds, will keep stalling drives. I'd project roughly 185-235 passing yards and 1.0-1.6 passing TDs a game, with 2-3.5 sacks and 12-25 rushing yards.

The swing is personnel. Egbuka's return restores his most-used target, and Godwin has been his most efficient one. A healthy line is what turns his long holds into completions instead of sacks. If both come back and the third-down offense finds a quick answer beyond screens, the top of those ranges is reachable. If the protection stays patched, he sits near the bottom.

confidence.note: Four games and 129 dropbacks, a three-game absence, his return on just 11 attempts, and key teammates out.
